findings.text: The phone measurement has only a BEFORE run. requirements.md asks for before and after, and measure/task.jsonl stops at "waiting for the AFTER instruction". Run the AFTER on the card page (Fast 3G), and land with both numbers side by side.

The BEFORE diagnostic (measure/task.jsonl) found that the phone waits on about 150 small requests, not on bytes. The new readers add requests: Markdown.js `walk()` (depth Infinity, one page.jsonl per folder) and ext/files/fs.js `list()` fetch a log for every sub-folder, so /fs/ or an md index on a big folder can mean hundreds or thousands of requests where there used to be one directory.json. Measure one big folder (for example /framework/ext/files/fs/ pointed at /framework/) before calling this a phone win, or cap the depth.

The review/shots/ folder is empty: none of the listed sheet.png files exist. So nothing here judges layout, order or navigation from pictures. The readers minion says its headless probe of 8 pages showed 0 directory.json fetches and 0 console errors. That is the only visual evidence.

The covered-folder rule (Server/plugins/PageFiles.js:124-141) still covers `assets/` and `img/` folders (public/assets/page.jsonl, public/assets/img/page.jsonl, ai2/doc/img/page.jsonl), which the brief suggested leaving out. The result is 2,407 new tracked files. The rule was applied without being shown to the owner as a proposal, even though the brief named "don't clutter the tree" as the concern.

From now on, creating any file under public/ appends a line to a git-tracked page.jsonl. Every new file therefore shows up as two changes in git. `merge=union` (.gitattributes:13) handles merges, but the noise in diffs and commits is new, and the owner should know about it.

The line format is not the one in requirements.md: it writes `{"file":"kid/"}` instead of `{"dir":"kid"}`, and `{"file":"x","gone":true}` instead of `{"removed":"x"}`. Reusing the existing format is the simpler choice, and core/Page/doc/jsonl.md documents it, but say so in the landing report so it doesn't read as a missed ask.

The Router's child lookup (core/Page/Page.class.js:225-240) only uses a listing that something else has already fetched (`loaded_listing`). It never fetches one itself, so requirement 4 is only partly met for the Router. The comment gives a reason (every folder would pay a fetch), and that reason is fair, but name it in the report.

PageFiles now appends file lines to folders that have a page.js, including imagine/cms/json/page.jsonl, whose log is also the CMS's own page data (jsonl.md, "A folder with a page.js is no longer skipped"). That works only while the CMS reader keeps ignoring `file` lines. It is worth a one-line check that /imagine/cms/json/ still renders and saves.

dev/DevBar/ask.js:62-81 and ext/drawer/tabs/sessions.js:27-45 now hold the same new `threads()` body, line for line. The simpler way is one exported function (sessions.js already exports it) that ask.js imports.

ai2/groups.js `day()` (line ~379) turns every folder in a day into a Member and calls `live()` on its task.jsonl, even folders with no task.jsonl. Before this change, only folders with a task.jsonl were read. This is harmless over the socket, but each empty folder is a wasted subscription. Filtering on the folder's own listing when it is already loaded would cost nothing.

The earlier readers review (readers/review.md #1: a log with no `file` lines is read as an empty folder, not as "no listing") is mostly moot now that the backfill has caught up every existing log. The comment on `listing()` at core/Page/Log.js:492 still says so plainly, so that one is fine as it stands.
